subject: Renewal: capacity top-up & model migration proposal
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice@soliq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: capacity top-up & model migration proposal

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the renewal signal last week. Per our call, I pulled together a proposal that covers the next 12 months and the two main asks you called out: (1) headroom for increased throughput during Black Friday peak, and (2) a model mix change to include a larger long-context generator + a two-stage re-ranking add-on.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Term: 12 months (auto-renew opt-out at 9 months)
- Reserved capacity: add 8 H100 GPUs to the existing dedicated pool (isolated pool for Soliq)
- Burst/throughput guarantee: baseline 80k tokens/sec reserved across the pool; guaranteed 95th pct latency SLO for 1k-token generations during peak windows
- Model mix: Convert 30% of baseline capacity to a 24k-context candidate generator (LlamaX-34B q4f16 variant) and add a dedicated 2-GPU reranker appliance (pairwise ranker, ~16k context) as an optional add-on at renewal pricing
- Price: preliminary pricing attached (see pricing_breakdown_Q4.xlsx) — includes a transition credit for model migration engineering and a one-time onboarding assistance credit

Attachments: Soliq_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf (SOW draft), pricing_breakdown_Q4.xlsx

Next steps: if this aligns, I can circulate a revised SOW with exact SLA language and a DocuSign envelope for signature. Monica and Karthik are looped for technical sizing and rollout timing.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for LLMs

From: Alice Turner <alice@soliq.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Soliq Commerce Procurement <procure@soliq.com>, EngOps Team <eng-ops@soliq.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity top-up & model migration proposal

Rachel —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. The lift generally looks like what we discussed. A few clarification items from EngOps and Procurement before we can move to SOW review:
1) Can you confirm the estimated GPU-hours / month for the 24k candidate generator projection? We need that to map to our internal cost center.
2) Procurement wants a current SOC 2 snapshot and a short note on data residency for logs during re-ranking steps. We will also run this against our vendor security questionnaire.
3) On the reranker: we are interested in a 2-stage flow you described, but want to understand whether it would live in the reserved pool or be a managed shared service. If reserved, what's the minimum GPU allocation and expected latency impact on our other workloads?

If you can answer above and send the SOC2 doc, we can get the SOW to legal and procurement this week.

Thanks —
Alice Turner
Head of Search & Relevance, Soliq Commerce
alice@soliq.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity top-up & model migration proposal

Rachel / team —

Quick technical breakdown to respond to Soliq:
- 24k candidate generator (LlamaX-34B q4f16) estimate: ~520 GPU-hours/month per replica at moderate traffic (this assumes aggressive prompt caching and continuous KV cache reuse). For 30% of baseline capacity mapped to two generator replicas, estimate ~1,040 GPU-hours/month.
- Reranker: a compact pairwise reranker (16k context) can run at ~1200 QPS on a 2x H100 reserved pair if we batch aggressively; realistic steady-state reserved allocation would be 2 GPUs for the dedicated reranker appliance. During Black Friday bursts, we can add burst capacity from a shared pool if Soliq approves bursting.
- Impact on other workloads: if we reserve 8 additional H100s and pin 2 for reranker, the remaining GPUs can be autoscaled for generator capacity. We should include a soft-affinity placement to ensure isolation for critical low-latency routes.

Attachments: pricing_breakdown_Q4.xlsx (updated with per-GPU-hour breakout)

I can draft a one-page technical appendix for the SOW with the above numbers plus fallback routing behavior. Monica — can you add the operational play (on-call, runbook note) for the reranker?

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice@soliq.com>, Soliq Commerce Procurement <procure@soliq.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: capacity top-up & model migration proposal

Alice / team —

Thanks for the questions — please see inline below and attached SOC2 snapshot.

> "Can you confirm the estimated GPU-hours / month for the 24k candidate generator projection?"
Karthik's estimate above is captured in the pricing sheet: ~1,040 GPU-hours/month for the two-replica generator mapping we proposed. We also included a sensitivity section that shows +/-30% utilization scenarios.

> "Procurement wants a current SOC 2 snapshot and a short note on data residency for logs during re-ranking steps."
Attached: SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf. Short note: log retention for reranking traces can be configured to remain in your VPC (private deployment) or redwood-managed encrypted storage in us-west-2. We can add a clause to the SOW that the customer retains ownership of application-level logs and that audit copies are retained for 90 days by default unless otherwise requested.

> "On the reranker: reserved vs shared service?"
We recommend reserved 2x H100s for the reranker appliance during the initial 12-month term to meet latency targets. Optionally, you can enable burst into Redwood shared capacity at a controlled rate — price shown in the attachment.

Next steps proposed:
1) We will incorporate the technical appendix and the SLO language into Soliq_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf and pull a DocuSign envelope for signature (link below).
2) Proposed start date: 2026-12-01 production switch; transition window begins 2026-11-10 for staging and validation.
3) Pricing and legal: draft SOW includes a one-time migration assistance credit of $35k applied at contract start.

DocuSign (proposal): https://docusign.com/prepare/RDW-4921-sign
SOW (draft): https://app.redwood.ai/docs/SOWs/RDW-DEAL-4921

If this looks good, please route to procurement and legal and we will prepare the final SOW for signature.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rachel / team —

Good summary — procurement and legal have reviewed the SOW and the SOC2 snapshot. We appreciate the migration credit and the explicit log residency language. A couple of final items but nothing blocking:
- Procurement requests a short amendment that allows a one-time term-extension (90 days) at current rates if our rollout is delayed due to internal validation.
- EngOps would like a short runbook entry for the reranker warmup sequence (Monica, is your team able to provide this by 10/07?).

Assuming you can add those two items, please send the DocuSign envelope and we'll sign. Target go-live 2026-12-01 looks good.

Thanks —
Alice Turner
